verdict.rationale: Cline's own docs say every action, including MCP tool use, goes through human-in-the-loop approval. Auto Approve lets the user choose which action categories, MCP tools among them, run without prompting, and the app can manage MCP servers and plugins. That gives real control over which external tools the agent uses, but the evidence shows approval gating and server management rather than an explicit allowlist or policy that restricts integration access. missing for 10: an explicit per-tool/per-server allow/deny configuration, team- or org-level enforcement of integration permissions, in-depth docs on MCP permission settings, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can control which external tools and integrations the agent is allowed to access

citations.quote: MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets Cline use external tools and data sources through MCP servers.
manage models, plugins, and MCP servers

Auto Approve lets you decide which actions Cline can take without prompting you each time. It keeps you out of approval popups during routine work while letting you keep tight control over high-risk actions.
Cline auto-approves everything: file changes, terminal commands, browser actions, MCP tools, and mode transitions.
Every action requires your explicit approval.
